text:
maya: FYI seeing a steady tail-latency drift in eu-west over the last 6h. not full noisy neighbor but a few tenants slowly inflating p99s. wondering if we try a 'quiet silo' pre-provision instead of full dedicated carveouts?
infra-bot: Alert: EU-WEST GPU p99 latency > 95th percentile for 6m (signal id: gw-eh-472).
alex: can you paste the metric window? curious which rack / pool.
maya: quick snippet from Grafana: ```
cluster: eu-west
pool: general-gpu
window: 06:00-12:00 UTC
p50: 42ms
p95: 210ms -> 345ms (gradual)
p99: 560ms -> 980ms
active tenants spiking: tenant-17, tenant-88
alloc rate stable
```
sam: hm tenants look low qps but high bursts. might be kvcache churn? any recent model rollouts?
maya: tenant-88 rolled a new quantized 7B at 02:30 but their token distribution is chatty. saw more small synchronous calls.
rishabh: noisy neighbor but not classic — it's a simmer: long-lived KV cache thrash that increases bus contention. full dedicated pool would fix but costs a lot.
maya: idea: create a 'quiet-silo' reservation that pre-allocates warm slots and isolates NVLink/PIO channels but does not give full dedicated billing. it's like soft-provisioning for suspect tenants to reduce tail without full carveouts.
anya: sounds interesting. what isolation surface do we need? NIC queue shaping + subtle GPU bus QoS?
alex: probably need allocator changes: mark slots with low sharing factor and pin to local GPU slices, bump nic qos for that slice, plus an eviction grace. also need fallback if it underutilizes.
sam: config sketch: ```
reserve_type: quiet-silo
slots: 4
isolation: [kv_cache_lockdown, nic_shaping]
billing: shared-lowcommit
fallback: revert-to-general after 30m idle
```
maya: also want routing rule: if p95 exceeds 300ms for >5m and tenant has repeated pattern, auto-enroll for 15m. roll back if p95 stable < 200ms.
rishabh: implications: we'd need telemetry flagging and a small SLA doc for customers (they get latency isolation but not throughput guarantees). ops question: how many concurrent quiet-silos can fleet sustain?
alex: short calc: each quiet-silo ~ 4 warm slots -> ~8% capacity hit per rack depending on oversubscription. need to test on staging.
anya: can we pilot in a specific rack group? maybe eu-west-rack-3 where the issue surfaced.
maya: i'll spin a canary job to simulate tenant-88 profile and run allocator changes in staging. will share results in the next 2 days.
infra-bot: Note: created ticket INF-9243 (quiet-silo experiment) and scheduled a canary window for 2819993600-2819997200 UTC.
alex: perfect. if it works, we'll prototype the admission controller + small console toggle. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks — assigning to sam + rishabh for the canary infra work. i'll handle tenant-sim workload.
sam: ack. starting checklists now.
rishabh: ack. i'll draft the telemetry and cost model for quiet-silos.
